model_note.S:
cc: Gradual tingling and numbness in both feet

HPI: 28 yo m. Patient reports: It started 4 months ago. It began in the toes of both feet. It has spread up to the ankles, not into my hands. It is tingling, burning and reduced feeling. Burning is 5/10 at night. It has gradually spread and is now present daily. There was no injury. Taking the bedsheet off my feet helps. The bedsheet touching my feet and nighttime worsen it. I tried a foot cream without benefit. I have not had this before. Both feet feel numb. They tingle and burn at night. I have been more thirsty lately.

Patient perspective: Will I lose my feet like someone I know?

PMH: Type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age 18,10 years ago; last A1c was high but does not recall the number.

PSH: No surgery or admissions.

Meds: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily; sometimes misses the evening dose.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink monthly. No recreational drugs. Cashier; lives with wife; eats an unrestricted diet.

FH: Mother had diabetes; father hypertension; brother healthy; no hereditary neuropathy known.

ROS: Neurologic - Reports numbness. Reports paresthesia. Denies weakness. General - Reports polydipsia. Denies weight loss. Denies fever. Gastrointestinal - Denies diarrhea. Denies constipation. Denies nausea.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.2 F oral, P 78 bpm, BP 136/82 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert and comfortable at rest.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

Neuro: Reduced light touch and vibration symmetrically from toes to ankles. Achilles reflexes reduced bilaterally; patellar reflexes 2+. Lower extremity strength 5/5 bilaterally.

Skin: Skin of feet intact, without visible ulceration.

Ext: Dorsalis pedis pulses palpable and symmetric.

Osteopathic: C1 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.
P: 1. Assess symmetric sensory loss, foot integrity and gait; obtain A1c and review diabetes management and renal function; discuss individualized neuropathic-pain treatment with clinician review, daily foot checks and protective footwear; follow up in 2–4 weeks and seek prompt care for wounds, rapidly progressive weakness or falls.
2. Check B12 and CBC, particularly with long-term metformin use; replace a confirmed deficiency and investigate its cause; explain that more than one contributor may coexist.

3. Review neurotoxic drugs, supplements and alcohol exposure; do not stop necessary medication without prescriber review; arrange further neurologic testing if the pattern is atypical or progresses. Refer to neurology for atypical or progressive deficits and consider nerve conduction studies when needed to clarify the pattern; educate the patient to review supplements and drug exposures with the prescribing clinician rather than stopping necessary treatment independently.

cc: Gradual tingling and numbness in both feet

HPI: 28 yo m. Patient reports: It started 7 months ago. It began in the toes of both feet. It has spread up to the ankles, not into my hands. It is tingling, burning and reduced feeling. Burning is 5/10 at night. It has gradually spread and is now present daily. There was no injury. Taking the bedsheet off my feet helps. The bedsheet touching my feet and nighttime worsen it. I tried a foot cream without benefit. I have not had this before. Both feet feel numb. They tingle and burn at night. I have been more thirsty lately.

Patient perspective: Will I lose my feet like someone I know?

PMH: Type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age 18,10 years ago; last A1c was high but does not recall the number.

PSH: No surgery or admissions.

Meds: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily; sometimes misses the evening dose.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink monthly. No recreational drugs. Cashier; lives with wife; eats an unrestricted diet.

FH: Mother had diabetes; father hypertension; brother healthy; no hereditary neuropathy known.

ROS: Neurologic - Reports numbness. Reports paresthesia. Denies weakness. General - Reports polydipsia. Denies weight loss. Denies fever. Gastrointestinal - Denies diarrhea. Denies constipation. Denies nausea.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.2 F oral, P 78 bpm, BP 136/82 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert and comfortable at rest.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

Neuro: Reduced light touch and vibration symmetrically from toes to ankles. Achilles reflexes reduced bilaterally; patellar reflexes 2+. Lower extremity strength 5/5 bilaterally.

Skin: Skin of feet intact, without visible ulceration.

Ext: Dorsalis pedis pulses palpable and symmetric.

Osteopathic: C1 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.
P: 1. Assess symmetric sensory loss, foot integrity and gait; obtain A1c and review diabetes management and renal function; discuss individualized neuropathic-pain treatment with clinician review, daily foot checks and protective footwear; follow up in 2–4 weeks and seek prompt care for wounds, rapidly progressive weakness or falls.
2. Check B12 and CBC, particularly with long-term metformin use; replace a confirmed deficiency and investigate its cause; explain that more than one contributor may coexist.

3. Review neurotoxic drugs, supplements and alcohol exposure; do not stop necessary medication without prescriber review; arrange further neurologic testing if the pattern is atypical or progresses. Refer to neurology for atypical or progressive deficits and consider nerve conduction studies when needed to clarify the pattern; educate the patient to review supplements and drug exposures with the prescribing clinician rather than stopping necessary treatment independently.
